raw_text:
Important: this plan starts at week 0–4 postpartum and follows OB guidance: light activity only, no abdominal exercises or heavy lifting until the 6‑week check. If at any point she has pain, heaviness in the pelvis, new or worsening bleeding, dizziness, or separation/ bulging in the midline with coughing or straining, stop exercise and advise medical review. Progress only with clinician clearance at the 6‑week check.

Overview and goals
- Primary goals: safely restore baseline fitness, re‑train pelvic floor and deep core (after clearance), rebuild general strength and endurance, improve posture and functional movement, manage fatigue and sleep, and support recovery/ breastfeeding nutrition.
- Equipment: yoga mat only. Use bodyweight, tempo and pain-free range. Emphasize posture, breathing, pelvic floor, progressive load after 6 weeks, and recovery.
- Structure: 12 weeks divided into three phases: Phase A (weeks 1–4, current to 6‑week check period — very gentle), Phase B (weeks 5–8, early strengthening after clearance), Phase C (weeks 9–12, build strength and return to higher workload). Four sessions per week (2 structured sessions + 1 active recovery walk + 1 mobility/relaxation session) — adjustable to client energy and breastfeeding schedule.

Precautions and screening cues
- Ask about pain, heaviness, bulging or urinary/fecal leakage during or after activity. If any, stop and refer to pelvic health physio.
- Monitor return of menses, sleep, nutrition and mood (postpartum mood disturbances common).
- Avoid Valsalva/holding breath; cue slow exhalation during exertion. Emphasize pelvic floor engagement with every exertion.
- Rest when needed; prioritize feeding/infant care schedule.

PHASE A — Weeks 1–4 (current to week 6 check): gentle reconditioning, breathing and pelvic floor prep
Goal: restore walking tolerance, improve posture, breath mechanics, start gentle pelvic floor activation (submaximal, not straining). No abdominal loading or trunk flexion/rotation.

Weekly structure (4 sessions/week)
- 3 short sessions (20–25 min): low‑impact mobility, breathing/pelvic floor practice, gentle strength for hips/glutes and scapular stabilizers.
- 1 longer walk session (20–30 min) at gentle pace; can split into two shorter walks.

Progression: increase duration and repetitions slowly as tolerated; keep intensity low (RPE 2–3/10).

Example week template (Weeks 1–4 — do similar each week, increase walk time + add 1–2 reps per exercise each week)

Session A — Mobility, breathing, pelvic floor (20–25 min)
1. Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor cueing: 5 minutes lying or seated. Inhale to belly/ribcage, gently lift pelvic floor on exhale (short, gentle contraction) — 6–8 reps, hold 1–2 seconds, breathe between. No breath‑holding.
2. Neck/chest mobility: chin tucks (8–10), gentle thoracic rotations seated (8 each side).
3. Scapular retraction/rows (standing T–to–Y progression): wall slides or prone Y/T if comfortable (10–12).
4. Glute activation: glute bridges (modify small range) 10–12 slow reps. Emphasize breathing and pelvic floor.
5. Side‑lying hip abduction (or standing) 10 each side.
6. Cat–cow (gentle) 8–10.
7. Pelvic floor quick squeezes: 8–10 quick, easy squeezes (not holding breath), then 3–4 gentle longer holds up to 5 seconds as tolerated.

Session B — Gentle strength + balance (20–25 min)
1. Warmup walk in place or march (3–5 min).
2. Split‑stance mini squats (box or chair to sit lightly) — shallow, 10–12. No Valsalva.
3. Heel raises (calf) 12–15 slow.
4. Bird‑dog (hands and knees) alternating, focus on neutral spine — 8 each side.
5. Clamshells (side‑lying) 10–12 each side.
6. Standing hip hinge to reach (finger‑tip tap to shin) — gentle, 8–10.
7. Finish with 5 minutes of pelvic floor breathing practice.

Walk session
- 20–30 minutes total at comfortable pace; split if needed (e.g., 10 + 10). Gradually build to 30 min by week 4.

Recovery/mobility session (15–20 min)
- Gentle stretching: hip flexors, pecs, lats, hamstrings.
- Short guided relaxation or progressive muscle relaxation (5–8 min).
- Foam rolling optional if available.

Nutrition & recovery guidance for Phase A
- Focus on adequate protein (~1.1–1.3 g/kg/day while breastfeeding; if not breastfeeding, 0.8–1.0 g/kg), energy to support healing and milk production, plenty of fluids.
- Prioritize sleep when possible; naps with baby and accept help.
- Encourage iron and vitamin intake as advised by OB (continue prenatal if recommended).
- Simple meal strategies: protein at each meal, snacks, easy balanced meals.

PHASE B — Weeks 5–8 (post 6‑week check onward; begin progressive core and strength)
Prerequisite: medical clearance at 6 weeks and no pelvic floor dysfunction signs. Begin controlled core reintroduction (not heavy loading), increase strength volume. Continue monitoring for diastasis recti (DR) and pelvic floor symptoms.

Weekly structure (4 sessions/week)
- 2 strength sessions (30–35 min)
- 1 conditioning walk (30–40 min or intervals)
- 1 mobility/pelvic floor/core session (20–25 min)

Progression: add sets, reps, increase ROM and complexity. Use slower tempos, focus on quality.

Session C — Strength 1 (Lower + core reactivation)
Warmup 5 min: marching, hip circles, shoulder rolls.
1. Box/assisted squat to chair — 3 sets x 10–12 reps (4‑2‑1 tempo: 4s down, 2s pause, 1s up). Cue exhale on concentric, pelvic floor engagement.
2. Glute bridge with single leg progression (alternate) — 3 x 8–10 each side (or 12 double‑leg).
3. Standing hip abduction with band alternative (or side leg raise) — 3 x 12 each side.
4. Bird‑dog with 3 second hold — 3 x 8 each side.
5. Side plank on knees (modified) 3 x 20–30s each side as tolerated (focus on breathing, pelvic floor).
6. Pelvic floor and TVA draw‑in practice supine (gentle): 2 sets x 8 holds 5s.

Session D — Strength 2 (Upper + posterior chain)
Warmup 5 min.
1. Wall push‑ups or incline push‑ups — 3 x 8–12.
2. Prone or supine prone Y/T (if comfortable) scapular work — 3 x 10–12.
3. Reverse lunges to support — 3 x 8 each leg.
4. Hip hinge/standing RDL with soft knee — 3 x 10 (focus on glutes and hamstrings).
5. Farmer‑carry style single‑arm hold using baby/towel/dumbbell substitute (if available) — 3 x 30s each side (light).
6. Core: Dead bug progressions (limit spine flexion intensity) 3 x 8 each side, with exhale on movement.

Conditioning walk
- 30–40 min steady or 2–3 intervals of faster pace 3–4 min with easy pace recovery.

Mobility/core/pelvic floor session
- Diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic floor cueing: 6–10 reps.
- Cat–cow, thoracic rotations, pec wall stretches.
- Gentle core re‑education: heel slides (if no bulging) 2 x 10, modified side plank holds, pelvic tilts 10–12.
- If DR present: teach safe modifications (no crunches; use coning/bulging monitoring; consult physio if significant).

Nutrition & recovery guidance for Phase B
- Continue protein focus (1.2–1.6 g/kg if breastfeeding and training).
- Ensure 250–500 kcal/day additional energy if breastfeeding and training (individualize).
- Iron and B12 if needed; prioritize whole foods, veggies, healthy fats.
- Sleep hygiene: short naps, partner support, scheduled rest days.

PHASE C — Weeks 9–12 (build strength, endurance; prepare for return to normal activities)
Goal: increase intensity, functional strength, begin higher‑load progressions (still bodyweight unless cleared for external loads), introduce more dynamic moves if comfortable.

Weekly structure (4 sessions/week)
- 2 strength sessions (35–45 min)
- 1 longer walk/hike or interval conditioning (40–45 min)
- 1 mobility/core session (25–30 min)

Progression: increase sets to 3–4, add unilateral loading, longer holds, higher rep ranges and tempo changes.

Session E — Strength 3 (Lower body emphasis)
Warmup 5–7 min.
1. Split squat (rear foot elevated optional) — 3 x 8–10 each leg.
2. Single‑leg glute bridge or elevated glute bridge — 3 x 10–12.
3. Bulgarian split squat progression (bodyweight) — 3 x 6–8 each side (progress as tolerated).
4. Hip hinge to single‑leg RDL progress — 3 x 8 each side (balance focus).
5. Core: progressive dead bug to half roll‑up (only if no bulging and good control) 3 x 8.
6. Farmer carry/suitcase carry (use baby carrier or household object safely) 3 x 40–60s.

Session F — Strength 4 (Upper + core)
Warmup.
1. Incline pushups or knee pushups — 3 x 8–12.
2. Bent over row alternative (single‑arm row with household item) — 3 x 10–12 each side.
3. Shoulder stability: plank shoulder taps from knees or full plank if tolerated — 3 x 20 taps.
4. Glute‑ham emphasis: reverse Nordic progression or hamstring curl alternatives — 3 x 8–10.
5. Core: side planks full or modified 3 x 30–45s, bird‑dog progress 3 x 8 each side.
6. Finish with pelvic floor strength set: 8 slow holds 6–8 s and 8 quick squeezes.

Conditioning walk/hike
- 40–45 min moderate pace or interval session (e.g., 5x3 min faster with 2 min easy).

Mobility/core/recovery
- Dynamic mobility, foam rolling, longer breathing/pelvic floor session and guided relaxation. Add postpartum yoga sequences if desired.

Nutrition & recovery guidance for Phase C
- Match energy to activity and breastfeeding needs — protein 1.2–1.8 g/kg depending on training intensity.
- Include anti‑inflammatory foods (omega‑3s), adequate calcium and vitamin D for bone health.
- Encourage structured meal prep, snacks for feeding sessions, and prioritize recovery days.

Monitoring, regressions and referrals
- If any urinary leakage, pelvic heaviness, back pain, or visible doming with core activity, regress to earlier phase, reduce intensity, and refer to pelvic health physiotherapist.
- For diastasis recti >2.5–3 cm or significant bulging, consult physiotherapy before advancing core load.
- If breastfeeding and mastitis/engorgement occur, allow rest and reduce upper body loading if painful.

Sample week progression summary
- Weeks 1–4: mostly mobility, pelvic floor breathing, short walks; build to 30 min walk; 2×20–25 min strength/mobility sessions + 1 walk + 1 recovery.
- Weeks 5–8: after 6‑week clearance, introduce progressive strength 2×/week, increase walk to 30–40 min, start light core work and pelvic floor strengthening.
- Weeks 9–12: increase intensity and complexity, 2 strength sessions with unilateral work, longer conditioning walks, and more targeted core progressions; by week 12 client should feel ready to reintroduce normal household lifting gradually and consider external load training if cleared and comfortable.

Practical coaching cues
- Breathe: exhale during effort, avoid bearing down.
- Pelvic floor: gentle lift before and during exertion; avoid over‑tense (relax between reps).
- Quality over quantity: slower controlled movements, neutral spine, avoid crunching.
- Breaks: allow more rests and split sessions around baby care.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week‑by‑week sheet with daily checkboxes.
- Provide videos/links for each exercise (or describe regressions/progressions).
- Tailor caloric/protein targets if you give weight, height, breastfeeding status and activity level.
